# PET SHOP BOYS

## Who are the Pet Shop Boys?

Pet Shop Boys are an electronic pop duo from England who formed in 1981, comprising of ex-Smash Hits writer Neil Francis Tennant (born July 10, 1954 in North Shields, Northumberland) and one-time architecture student Christopher Sean Lowe (born 4 October 1959 in Blackpool).

The duo launched their career with the rerecorded West End Girls in 1985 which became the first of four Number 1s for the Pet Shop Boys, and also topped the Billboard charts.  In May 2024 Official Charts also revealed [West End Girls to be Pet Shop Boys' most-streamed song of all time too](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/pet-shop-boys-official-most-streamed-songs-in-the-uk/ "Pet Shop Boys' most-streamed songs"). Pet Shop Boys are the most successful duo in UK music history, racking up sales of in excess of 100 million, and the recipients of three BRIT Awards for Best Single (West End Girls in 1987), Best Group (1988) and an Outstanding Contribution to Music in 2009.

They have also won Outstanding Contribution to British Music at the Ivor Novello Awards in 2000. They’ve worked with, collaborated and remixed the likes of Dusty Springfield, Liza Minelli, Elton John, Robbie Williams, David Bowie and Madonna.

On 3 May 2024 [Nonetheless](https://www.officialcharts.com/albums/pet-shop-boys-nonetheless/) landed as the week's highest new entry on the Official Albums Chart at Number 2, Pet Shop Boys' highest-charting LP in 31 years, since [Very](https://www.officialcharts.com/albums/pet-shop-boys-very/) topped the chart in 1993.

## [Gwen Stefani Biography](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/mn0000546214\#biography "Gwen Stefani Biography")

### Gwen Stefani Biography  by   [David Jeffries](https://www.allmusic.com/author/david-jeffries "View more by David Jeffries")

[![Tragic Kingdom](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0000357753/front/220/_Nna1igoD1QMss_9ONgfTypQg_7iAU1wjqLgK_xGXts=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/tragic-kingdom-mw0000179531 "Tragic Kingdom")
Gwen Stefani has parlayed her breakout stardom as the effervescent lead singer of the SoCal ska-punk outfit [No Doubt](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/no-doubt-mn0000341672) into an enduring career as a multifaceted pop star. Before going solo, Stefani reached the top of the charts many times during [No Doubt](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/no-doubt-mn0000341672)'s peak. "Spiderwebs," "Just a Girl," and the ballad "Don't Speak" -- all pulled from their 1995 album [Tragic Kingdom](https://www.allmusic.com/album/tragic-kingdom-mw0000179531) \-\- were iconic alternative rock hits. The early-2000s smashes "Hey Baby," "Hella Good," and "Underneath It All" found the group dabbling in pop, dance, and R&B, a musical expansion that coincided with Stefani stepping outside of the band as a featured vocalist on the hits "South Side" by techno superstar [Moby](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/moby-mn0000477116) and "Let Me Blow Ya Mind" by the rapper [Eve](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/eve-mn0000150962). All this extracurricular activity helped set up the launch of Stefani's solo career in 2004 with the album [Love.Angel.Music.Baby.](https://www.allmusic.com/album/loveangelmusicbaby-mw0000258810), a platinum blockbuster that gave her a number one single with the thumping [Neptunes](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/neptunes-mn0000401903) collaboration "Hollaback Girl," plus the hits "Cool," "What You Waiting For?," and "Rich Girl," the latter a reunion with [Eve](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/eve-mn0000150962). The 2006 record [The Sweet Escape](https://www.allmusic.com/album/the-sweet-escape-mw0000445374) consolidated her pop success thanks to the Top Tens "Wind It Up" and "The Sweet Escape," but by that point, Stefani began to venture outside of music. She launched her fashion line L.A.M.B. in 2004, a pursuit she'd develop over the coming decade. She started to dabble in film, an interest that eventually led her to joining the televised singing competition The Voice in 2014 (where she met husband [Blake Shelton](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/blake-shelton-mn0000046814)). Music remained essential to Stefani's appeal -- she reunited with [No Doubt](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/no-doubt-mn0000341672) and returned to her solo career with 2016's Billboard 200-topping [This Is What the Truth Feels Like](https://www.allmusic.com/album/this-is-what-the-truth-feels-like-mw0002917797). Later singles, such as the contemporary country-influenced "Purple Irises" with [Shelton](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/shelton-mn0000046814), off 2024's [Bouquet](https://www.allmusic.com/album/bouquet-mw0004379135), along with her position on The Voice, reinforced her crossover pop legacy as a star who shines upon every aspect of the entertainment industry.

Born and raised in Fullerton, California, Stefani had a musical epiphany at the age of 17. She had fallen in love with the [Madness](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/madness-mn0000195874) and [Selecter](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/selecter-mn0000504276) records her brother [Eric](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/eric-mn0000190781) was constantly spinning. Seeing [Fishbone](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/fishbone-mn0000796045), [the Untouchables](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/the-untouchables-mn0000479546), and other bands involved in Los Angeles' ska revival scene only reinforced her interest, so she was more than ready when her brother asked her to join a ska band he was forming with a friend named [John Spence](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/john-spence-mn0001254015). ## [The Christmas Album Review by AllMusic](https://www.allmusic.com/album/the-christmas-album-mw0000192771\#review "The Christmas Album Review by AllMusic")

### The Christmas Album Review by   [Lindsay Planer](https://www.allmusic.com/author/lindsay-planer "View more by Lindsay Planer")

After three consecutive Top Five Pop albums in 1970 alone, it was somewhat of a no-brainer that Motown would want to include a holiday long-player to that list. The Jackson 5's Christmas Album (1970) combines classic favorites as well as a handful of compositions penned by [the Corporation](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/the-corporation-mn0001344074). This all-star team of Motown staffers and musicians boasted composer [Bobby Taylor](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/bobby-taylor-mn0000374639), [Deke Richards](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/deke-richards-mn0000814546) (guitar), [Freddie Perren](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/freddie-perren-mn0000798759) (keyboard), [Fonce Mizell](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/fonce-mizell-mn0000150046) (keyboards), and label co-founder [Berry Gordy](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/berry-gordy-mn0000047893). As they had done for each of the Jackson 5's previous platters, they carefully crafted and significantly modernized familiar seasonal selections. Leading off the effort is an unusual (for a pop act, anyway) two-part interpretation of "Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas," commencing with a fairly rote reading before kicking into high gear during a fittingly R&B-inspired coda. They follow with an undeniably soulful update of "Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town" and the fun and funky "Up on the Rooftop," which also adds instrumental elements of their hit "The Love You Save" with a few bars of "Here Comes Santa Claus" likewise worked into the mix. "Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer" is another standard that has been infused with a fresh spirit, once again yielding a well-chosen and adeptly executed revision. ## Happy Xmas (War Is Over) Review by   [William Ruhlmann](https://www.allmusic.com/author/william-ruhlmann "View more by William Ruhlmann")

The Beatles never released a commercial Christmas record during their career, though they recorded holiday messages for their fan club each year. With the group disbanded, former Beatle John Lennon determined to make a Christmas record in 1971, combining the seasonal sentiments with his antiwar activism. In December 1969, Lennon and his wife, Yoko Ono, had put up billboard advertisements in major cities around the world declaring, "War is over! (If you want it)," and they reiterated this statement two years later in their Christmas song "Happy Xmas (War Is Over)." Characteristically, Lennon was not going to let his listeners off the hook, even if it was holiday time. "And so this is Christmas," he sang, "and what have you done?" Employing a slow tempo and an elaborate arrangement and production devised by Phil Spector, the song delivered a message of holiday greeting and antiwar political sentiments. Released as a single in December 1971, "Happy Xmas (War Is Over)" reached the Top 40 on regular record charts as well as placing high in the Christmas charts, to which it returned upon reissue in 1972, 1983, 1984, and 1985. In England, the single was not released until 1972, when it reached the Top Five, returning to the charts in 1975, 1980, 1981, and 1982. Gradually, the song began to be accepted as a seasonal standard, a development hastened by covers recorded by the likes of such mainstream artists as Neil Diamond (who replaced "Xmas" in the title with "Christmas") in 1992 and Celine Dion in 1998.

# WHEN A CHILD IS BORN  by [JOHNNY MATHIS](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/28869/johnny-mathis/)

* * *

Texas-born singer Johnny Mathis released his first single in 1956, and made his UK chart debut in 1958 with the song Teacher Teacher and had his first Christmas hit that year with a version of Winter Wonderland. Entering the UK chart in November 1976, When A Child Is Born’s original melody was Soleado, a tune from 1974 by Ciro Dammicco (alias Zacar) who was the composer for Italy's Daniel Sentacruz Ensemble, and Dario Baldan Bembo.

Based on Damicco's earlier tune Le rose blu, published in 1972, the English language lyrics were written a few years later by Fred Jay, and was first performed by German singer Michael Holm in 1974 before Johnny Mathis got wind of it. Denying Showaddywaddy the coveted UK Official Singles Chart Christmas Number 1 spot with their version of Under The Moon Of Love, When A Child Is Born hit the top during Christmas week and remained there for three weeks

# QUEEN

## Who are Queen?

British rock band Queen were founded in 1970, originally comprised frontman Freddie Mercury (lead vocals, piano), Brian May (guitar, vocals), John Deacon (bass guitar), and Roger Taylor (drums, vocals).

Across their career, Queen have notched up a staggering six Number 1 singles and ten Number albums. Queen's Greatest Hits is the UK's [best-selling album of all time](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/the-best-selling-albums-of-all-time-on-the-official-uk-chart__15551/ "best-selling albums of all time").

Queen made their Official Chart debut in 1974 with the Top 10 hit Seven Seas Of Rhye, follow-up single Killer Queen became their first Top 5 hit, peaking at Number 2. The following year saw the release of perhaps their most famous song, the epic Bohemian Rhapsody - their first UK Number 1 single and one of the [best-selling songs of all time](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/the-best-selling-singles-of-all-time-on-the-official-uk-chart__21298/ "best-selling singles of all time"). Bohemian Rhapsody has earned the extremely rare accolade of being the coveted UK [Christmas Number 1](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/every-official-christmas-number-1-ever-__3618/ "every Christmas Number 1 single") twice, both in 1975 and again in 1991 following the passing of Freddie Mercury.

Sam Ryder Biography by [Timothy Monger](https://www.allmusic.com/author/timothy-monger "View more by Timothy Monger") [![The Sun's Gonna Rise](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0005484301/front/220/XtL5mz20LfRPfsdAjgDvQByhM-OFI8zG4l-qVpXXB1I=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/the-suns-gonna-rise-mw0003583504 "The Sun's Gonna Rise") Sam Ryder is an English singer/songwriter and social media personality who began his career in the hard rock and metal circuits, fronting groups like [the Morning After](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/the-morning-after-mn0001717145) and [Blessed by a Broken Heart](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/blessed-by-a-broken-heart-mn0001005044) before starting a solo career as a pop artist. Wielding his versatile and dynamic vocal range, he parlayed an unexpected bout of viral success into a major-label deal and debuted in early 2021 with powerful pop-driven singles like "Whirlwind" and "More." They were included on his first EP, [The Sun's Gonna Rise](https://www.allmusic.com/album/the-suns-gonna-rise-mw0003583504), before the end of the year. 2022 was a landmark year in Ryder's career which brought him both a runner-up spot at the Eurovision Song Contest and a U.K. number two placing for his co-composition "Space Man" which anchored his chart-topping album, [There's Nothing But Space, Man!](https://www.allmusic.com/album/theres-nothing-but-space-man%21-mw0003721895). After notching a holiday hit with 2023's "You're Christmas to Me," Ryder issued his earthier, soul-leaning sophomore album, [Heartland](https://www.allmusic.com/album/heartland-mw0004590630), in 2025. [![Feel the Power](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0003544295/front/220/NMa1I1EV7Oe1N6Wd_HQR35hUoDg0hsvx4F4sL4oO-nA=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/feel-the-power-mw0002278585 "Feel the Power") Raised in Essex, Ryder grew up admiring the vocal power and range of English rock titans like [Freddie Mercury](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/freddie-mercury-mn0000130028) and [Iron Maiden](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/iron-maiden-mn0000098465)'s [Bruce Dickinson](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/bruce-dickinson-mn0000527024). He taught himself to play guitar, but it was his impressive voice that became his ticket into the music industry. After recording a couple of albums with symphonic metal band [the Morning After](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/the-morning-after-mn0001717145), he was recruited by Canadian glam metal outfit [Blessed by a Broken Heart](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/blessed-by-a-broken-heart-mn0001005044) to become their frontman. He was a key part of the band's 2012 LP [Feel the Power](https://www.allmusic.com/album/feel-the-power-mw0002278585), and after parting ways in 2013 he tried his luck in Nashville, writing songs and pitching himself to labels. He even recorded a 2016 full-length that never saw the light of day. During the COVID-19 lockdown of 2020, he casually tried a more spontaneous route, posting short a cappella videos of himself singing hit songs on the Internet. Drawn in by his soulful powerhouse voice, he soon developed a following and was signed by Parlophone, which issued his debut single, "Whirlwind," in early 2021. Against atmospheric backdrops, additional singles like "Tiny Riots" and "More" combined his hard rock chops with pop hooks. These songs and more were collected on the EP [The Sun's Gonna Rise](https://www.allmusic.com/album/the-suns-gonna-rise-mw0003583504) in September 2021. Ryder's career enjoyed a significant boost when he was handed the opportunity to represent the U.K. at the 2022 Eurovision Song Contest. His song "Space Man" -- co-written with [Amy Wadge](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/amy-wadge-mn0001854108) and [Max Wolfgang](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/max-wolfgang-mn0003518186) \-\- finished second in the competition, giving the U.K. their best result at the ceremony since 1998. Subsequently, the track hit number two in the U.K. singles chart, and reached the Top 30 in eight other territories. He followed this success with the August 2022 single "Somebody" and both these tracks ultimately appeared on his chart-topping debut solo album, [There's Nothing But Space, Man!](https://www.allmusic.com/album/theres-nothing-but-space-man%21-mw0003721895), that November. Ryder's 2023 holiday track "You're Christmas to Me" reached number two on the U.K. singles chart and earned him a Brit Award nomination. During the front half of 2025, he began the buildup to his sophomore album with singles like "White Lie" and "Oh OK." Recorded in Nashville, it marked a change in his sound, mixing Hollywood and cinematic Western influences with R&B in a style he referred to as "frontier soul." [Heartland](https://www.allmusic.com/album/heartland-mw0004590630) was released in October of that year. ## [Sam Ryder Discography](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/sam-ryder-mn0001088134\#discography "Sam Ryder Discography") Main AlbumsSingles & EPsAll Year (Oldest to Newest)Year (Newest to Oldest)AllMusic Rating (Highest to Lowest)AllMusic Rating (Lowest to Highest)User Ratings (Highest to Lowest)User Ratings (Lowest to Highest)Album Title (A-Z)Album Title (Z-A) | | Year | Credit | AllMusic Rating | User Rating | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [![There's Nothing but Space, Man!](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0005671198/front/120/XH9XXr542n_liIuOFqca-YAf7E_1E-2MlBBPmPAXRBU=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/theres-nothing-but-space-man%21-mw0003721895 "There's Nothing but Space, Man!") | 2022 | [There's Nothing but Space, Man!](https://www.allmusic.com/album/theres-nothing-but-space-man%21-mw0003721895 "There's Nothing but Space, Man!")

## [Blossoms Biography](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/blossoms-mn0003457444\#biography "Blossoms Biography")

### Blossoms Biography  by   [Neil Z. Yeung](https://www.allmusic.com/author/neil-z-yeung "View more by Neil Z. Yeung")

[![Cool Like You](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0004867556/front/220/-hxcWU6FL41wvd-OXa0Ypd_M69_UI9rrJSVvWL2-yAg=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/cool-like-you-mw0003159621 "Cool Like You")
English quintet Blossoms burst onto the British scene in the 2010s, quickly rising from local clubs to festival stages within a few short years. Their breakthrough debut landed in 2016 after years of anticipation, topping charts and winning fans with a catchy, synth-forward blend of Brit-pop and indie rock heard on songs like hit single "Charlemagne." Incorporating more new wave influences on their follow-up, 2018's [Cool Like You](https://www.allmusic.com/album/cool-like-you-mw0003159621), the band maintained their presence on U.K. charts and on the touring circuit. By the end of the decade, they were selling out shows, including one at a hometown stadium. The group entered a new decade in 2020 with their third LP, the lovelorn [Foolish Loving Spaces](https://www.allmusic.com/album/foolish-loving-spaces-mw0003338258). They soon followed with 2022's [Ribbon Around the Bomb](https://www.allmusic.com/album/ribbon-around-the-bomb-mw0003660277).

Formed in Stockport by school chums [Tom Ogden](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/tom-ogden-mn0003422968) (vocals, guitar) and [Joe Donovan](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/joe-donovan-mn0003506047) (drums), Blossoms later incorporated [Charlie Salt](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/charlie-salt-mn0003422909) (bass, vocals), [Josh Dewhurst](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/josh-dewhurst-mn0003422937) (guitar), and [Myles Kellock](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/myles-kellock-mn0003422955) (keyboards, vocals) to round out their lineup. Their sound was pigeonholed as psych-pop, which the band didn't like; rather, they hit a sweet spot between [the Doors](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/the-doors-mn0000114342) and [Arctic Monkeys](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/arctic-monkeys-mn0000325357), combining a knack for classic pop songwriting and moody organ atmospherics with a youthful energy. [Ogden](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/ogden-mn0003422968)'s delivery occupied the space between [Richard Ashcroft](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/richard-ashcroft-mn0000290853) ( [the Verve](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/the-verve-mn0000575522)) and [Alex Turner](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/alex-turner-mn0000934227), of the aforementioned [Monkeys](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/monkeys-mn0000325357), as the group slithered from spooky, groovy warmth to peppy Brit-pop. Debut single "You Pulled a Gun on Me" was a fine example of this combination, and the band continued to develop on subsequent singles "Blow" and "Cut Me and I'll Bleed."

[![Blown Rose EP](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0004445643/front/220/JXu5WjPPLXdQVrLs-fzCTD6KsMttLlyBmmVTZ6_CLs0=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/blown-rose-ep-mw0002867126 "Blown Rose EP")
2015 saw the release of two EPs -- [Blown Rose](https://www.allmusic.com/album/blown-rose-mw0002867126) and [Charlemagne](https://www.allmusic.com/album/charlemagne-mw0002892503). As Blossoms gained exposure, they released another EP, [At Most a Kiss](https://www.allmusic.com/album/at-most-a-kiss-mw0002907380), in February 2016. The four-song set featured some new elements in the band's sound, including prominent synths and a more driving urgency. A month later, the group revealed plans for their debut full-length. The self-titled [Blossoms](https://www.allmusic.com/album/blossoms-mw0002947404) was released in summer 2016, topping U.K. and Scottish charts. Months later, they bolstered the effort with an extended edition that included ten additional songs.

[![In Isolation](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0005242001/front/220/CFduE_ICs2WchbyaiDEM3phUoDg0hsvx4F4sL4oO-nA=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/in-isolation-mw0003403967 "In Isolation")
In early 2018, Blossoms issued the singles "I Can't Stand It" and "There's a Reason Why (I Never Returned Your Calls)," which both appeared on their sophomore effort, [Cool Like You](https://www.allmusic.com/album/cool-like-you-mw0003159621), an even more pop-leaning record that arrived in April. The band continued to build a devoted fan base, selling out shows across the country. Their third LP arrived in January 2020. Titled [Foolish Loving Spaces](https://www.allmusic.com/album/foolish-loving-spaces-mw0003338258), the project's lyrical focus centered on themes of love and attachment, adopting a sound inspired by [Talking Heads](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/talking-heads-mn0000131650) and [U2](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/u2-mn0000219203), and gave them their second U.K. chart-topper. 2020's COVID-19 lockdown saw the band digitally release the remotely recorded [In Isolation](https://www.allmusic.com/album/in-isolation-mw0003403967), a stop-gap which included reworkings of some of their own songs and covers of tunes by [Babybird](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/babybird-mn0000073668), [Elvis Costello](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/elvis-costello-mn0000058549), and [the Beatles](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/the-beatles-mn0000754032), and a recording of a show [Live from the Plaza Theatre, Stockport](https://www.allmusic.com/album/live-from-the-plaza-theatre-stockport-mw0003407695); the two were bundled together for a physical release. 2022 brought Blossoms' fourth

# Aled Jones biography

![Aled Jones](https://www.bbc.com/staticarchive/c88fc5999e1a9ff8987b90c472abd24d9a4a48a0.jpg)

Last updated: 05 November 2009

In the mid 1980s Aled Jones, the boy treble with the pudding bowl haircut, was seemingly ubiquitous.

Aled was born on 29 December 1970 in Llandegfan, Anglesey. He joined the Bangor Cathedral Choir aged nine, and won many national singing competitions and Eisteddfodau.

He was first recorded by the Welsh company Sain, who were alerted to his talents by a member of the Bangor Cathedral congregation. An invitation followed from BBC Wales to sing the Angel in Handel's oratorio Jephtha with the BBC Welsh Symphony Orchestra and Chorus. Following the broadcast on BBC Two, BBC Wales was commissioned to make three TV specials for Christmas and Easter with Aled and the Chorus on location in Israel. Watched by over 18 million viewers, highlights were issued in 1985 on VHS and on record and many other TV appearances followed.

In July 1985, the BBC issued his rendition of Memory from Andrew Lloyd Webber's Cats. It wasn't a huge success, but his recording of Walking In The Air was a top five smash.

The song became forever associated with Christmas, due to being featured in the evergreen Raymond Briggs animation The Snowman. It made Aled a huge international star, although it wasn't his voice on the film but that of Peter Auty. He appeared on Top Of The Pops, performed with legendary composer/conductor Leonard Bernstein and sang with the Los Angeles Philharmonic Orchestra in front of 27,000 people. Less fortunate was the occasion when he forgot the words to Memory while singing for the Queen - an occasion which reportedly caused him nightmares for some years afterwards.

While Aled wasn't able to repeat the phenomenal popular success of Walking In The Air, he released a number of albums between 1985 and 87 - mostly containing religious music and traditional songs - which earned him numerous gold and platinum discs. He even became the first person ever to have two classical albums in the pop charts simultaneously.

And then he disappeared from the public eye. The problem was, as is so often the case, hormones. For unlike that other famous Welsh angel, [Charlotte Church](https://www.bbc.com/wales/music/sites/charlotte-church/), Aled had to overcome the adolescent problem of the broken voice. Opera star [Stuart Burrows](https://www.bbc.com/wales/music/sites/stuart-burrows/) advised him to not sing for five years once his voice broke, but still Aled found it hard to stop.

He became a county level tennis player, and studied at the Royal Academy of Music where he joined jazz-funk band A2Z. He went on to gain entry at the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School, where he trained as an actor. It led to appearances in productions of Twelfth Night and Joseph And His Amazing Technicolour Dreamcoat.

He has become a regular presenter/performer on Songs Of Praise and presents his own shows on BBC Radio 2, Radio 3 and Radio Wales. And, to the delight of many, he's returned to recording music. In 2002 he signed a five album deal with Universal, the first of which, Aled, went platinum and the second, Higher, achieved gold within weeks.

In addition to all his recording and presenting commitments, Aled has found time to write his autobiography, fit in solo touring and compete in Strictly Come Dancing, in which he came fourth in 2004.

Aled's subsequent recordings include , [The Christmas Album](https://www.bbc.com/wales/music/sites/aled-jones/pages/christmas-album.shtml) and You Raise Me Up: The Best Of Aled Jones, in which he re-recorded Walking In The Air with himself as a treble - bringing his career full-circle.

In 2010 Aled issued another Christmas album, Aled's Christmas Gift and a book about his favourite Christmas carols.

# Bon Jovi releases new holiday tune 'Christmas Isn't Christmas': Listen here

'The Right Stuff’ for holiday entertaining

Jeff Kravitz/Getty Images for iHeartMedia, FILE

By[Jill Lances](https://abcnews.comauthor/jill_lances)

November 17, 2023, 3:03 PM

Bon Jovi has given fans a new tune to enjoy this holiday season.

The band just released the new song "Christmas Isn't Christmas," on which frontman Jon Bon Jovi laments how the holidays are not the same if a loved one isn't there.

"'Christmas Isn't Christmas' is a song that I wrote about family," the rocker shared in a statement. "The sentiment that Christmas really isn't Christmas without YOU which can bring up a lot of memories for people. I also liked to turn it around and know that because of you Christmas IS Christmas."

## [The Darkness Biography](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/mn0000141683\#biography "The Darkness Biography")

### The Darkness Biography  by   [Eduardo Rivadavia](https://www.allmusic.com/author/eduardo-rivadavia "View more by Eduardo Rivadavia")

[![Permission to Land](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0000874864/front/220/gTKfoPpm7JwmRBpG9oFd1SpQg_7iAU1wjqLgK_xGXts=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/permission-to-land-mw0000692543 "Permission to Land")
Overblown with pomp and camp, England's the Darkness crash the pop mainstream, resurrecting classic rock & roll bombast and tongue-in-cheek excess. Heralded by the anthemic single "I Believe in a Thing Called Love," 2003's [Permission to Land](https://www.allmusic.com/album/permission-to-land-mw0000692543) proved a banner debut, scoring armfuls of awards and chart records. The band imploded just as abruptly as they seemed to arrive, breaking up after their sophomore release, 2005's [One Way Ticket to Hell...And Back](https://www.allmusic.com/album/one-way-ticket-to-helland-back-mw0000703412). New bands were formed, rehab was completed, and old wounds were healed in the years that followed. The band reunited in 2011 and issued their comeback, [Hot Cakes](https://www.allmusic.com/album/hot-cakes-mw0002393712), in 2012. Subsequent 2010s efforts expanded their reliably raucous and nostalgia-indebted hard rock catalog, capturing fans with their theatrical live shows and devotion to excess and wry humor. At the turn of the decade, they released [Easter Is Cancelled](https://www.allmusic.com/album/easter-is-cancelled-mw0003309950) (2019) and [Motorheart](https://www.allmusic.com/album/motorheart-mw0003576298) (2021). Their eighth effort, [Dreams on Toast](https://www.allmusic.com/album/dreams-on-toast-mw0004383050), arrived in 2025.

The Darkness is centered around irrepressible frontman [Justin Hawkins](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/justin-hawkins-mn0001322080) (vocals/guitars/keyboards), who, along with his guitar-playing baby brother [Dan](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/dan-mn0001523163), bassist [Frankie Poullain](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/frankie-poullain-mn0002162806), and drummer [Ed Graham](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/ed-graham-mn0001388914), single-handedly resurrected the rather unfashionable sounds and attitudes of late-'70s hard rock for an unsuspecting generation. Following the demise of an earlier, conspicuously synth pop-based outfit named Empire, the Hawkins brothers sowed the seeds of what would become the Darkness at an impromptu karaoke session on New Year's Eve 1999. [Justin](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/justin-mn0001322080)'s rapturous rendition of [Queen](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/queen-mn0000858827)'s "Bohemian Rhapsody" showed them the way, and the suitably dramatic name "the Darkness" was chosen shortly after the arrival of [Poullain](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/poullain-mn0002162806) and [Graham](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/graham-mn0001388914).

With outrageous stage antics that included gaudy leotards stolen from [Steven Tyler](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/steven-tyler-mn0000049797)'s wardrobe, leaps and splits borrowed from [David Lee Roth](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/david-lee-roth-mn0000222436), and an ear-piercing falsetto copped from [Freddie Mercury](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/freddie-mercury-mn0000130028) himself, the multi-talented elder [Hawkins](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/hawkins-mn0001322080) led the quartet as the group spent the next two years slogging it out on London's pub circuit. Though they were immediately singled out as a joke by the notoriously vicious British press, the Darkness' high-energy sets, remarkably catchy material, and unapologetic worship of old-school rock & roll bombast gradually earned them a fanatical following based on simple word of mouth.

[![I Believe in a Thing Called Love [EP]](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0002245159/front/220/hLvKcBEhf7HjqpEOVxJ6clWnbEN5fCjifro6xhIBuB4=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/i-believe-in-a-thing-called-love-ep--mw0001308606 "I Believe in a Thing Called Love [EP]")
The tide finally began to shift in their favor in August 2002, when the band released their debut EP, [I Believe in a Thing Called Love](https://www.allmusic.com/album/i-believe-in-a-thing-called-love-mw0001308606) (through the independent label Must Destroy Music), won a major talent contest, and sc

## Who are WHAM?

Wham! were one of the biggest pop groups of the 1980s; comprising schoolmates [George Michael](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/3/george-michael/ "George Michael's chart history") and Andrew Ridgeley. In their original 4-year time-span, Wham! scored four UK Number 1 singles and ignited a deep and passionate fan base both in the UK and US with hits like Wake Me Up Before You Go Go, Club Tropicana and The Edge of Heaven.

For several decades Wham! also laid claim to the best-selling single of all time that had never reached Number 1, their perennial favourite Last Christmas originally got pipped to the top spot by the blockbusting charity single Band Aid upon release in Christmas 1984 but still went on to become one of the UK's much-loved and most successful hits in history. However, in 2021 that claim was eradicated when Wham!'s festive classic did finally get its moment of glory, reaching Number 1 on the Official Singles Chart a whole 36 years after the song's release. In doing so, Last Christmas became Wham!'s fifth UK Number 1 single.

On 22 December 2023, WHAM! made Official Chart history, when, 39 years in the making, [Last Christmas finally landed the coveted UK Christmas Number 1](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/christmas-number-1-2023-wham-last-christmas-makes-chart-history-andrew-ridgeley/ "Christmas Number 1 2023 - WHAM Last Christmas"), marking the longest journey ever to Christmas Number 1. With 13.3 million streams in seven days, it also set a new record for the most-streamed Christmas Number 1 ever in Christmas week. WHAM's Last Christmas also managed to become the [2024 Christmas Number 1](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/christmas-number-1-2024-whams-last-christmas-makes-official-chart-history-again-andrew-ridgeley/ "Christmas number 1 2024"), breaking Official Chart records as the first song in history to secure the Christmas Number 1 in consecutive years.

# TOO MUCH  by [SPICE GIRLS](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/1633/spice-girls/)

* * *

The sixth consecutive UK Official Singles Chart Number 1 for the Scary, Sporty, Posh, Baby and Ginger – the first act in chart history to do so – and their second consecutive UK Official Singles Chart Christmas Number 1, Too Much was their big ballad from their album, and opening song from their film, Spiceworld.

Based on an original idea by Geri, Too Much was co-written by the girls with the production team Absolute (Andy Watkins and Paul Wilson) in July 1997, while they were filming Spiceworld. The schedule being what it was, the group usually went straight into a mobile recording studio set up in a Winnebago, which followed them between film sets. Released December 15, 1997, Too Much entered the chart at the top spot in time to become 1997’s UK Official Singles Chart Christmas Number 1, staying there for a fortnight at the start of a 19-week chart run.

![Kelly Clarkson and Ariana Grande](https://www.billboard.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Kelly-Clarkson-Ariana-Grande-billboard-1548.jpg?w=942&h=628&crop=1)

Kelly Clarkson and Ariana GrandeTrae Patton/NBC/NBCU Photo Bank via Getty Images

### Trending on Billboard

Santa’s elves work hard, but [Ariana Grande](https://www.billboard.com/artist/ariana-grande/) and [Kelly Clarkson](https://www.billboard.com/artist/kelly-clarkson/) work harder. On Friday (Dec. 2), the two singers and former _Voice_ coaches released a live recording of their holiday duet “Santa, Can’t You Hear Me,” originally performed last year during Clarkson’s NBC Christmas special.

### Related

[![Lizzo](https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/ariana-grande-kelly-clarkson-drop-santa-cant-you-hear-me-live-version-1235180169/)\\

\\
**Lorde Calls Out Robert Kraft in ‘Free Palestine’ Jacket Following Ed Sheeran, Macklemore Tour Controversy**](https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/lorde-shades-robert-kraft-free-palestine-jacket-acl-1236354957/)

[![ADÉLA photographed on September 18, 2026 at Brooklyn Steel in Brooklyn.](https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/ariana-grande-kelly-clarkson-drop-santa-cant-you-hear-me-live-version-1235180169/)\\
\\
**Chartbreaker: Why ‘Everybody Wants To Root For’ ADÉLA**](https://www.billboard.com/music/pop/adela-aint-in-la-october-2026-chartbreaker-interview-1236349602/)

The new live version of “Santa, Can’t You Hear Me” serves as a follow up to the studio recording featured on Clarkson’s album _When Christmas Comes Around…_, released in October 2021. Peaking at No. 22 on the [Billboard 200](https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-200), the project marked the three-time Grammy winner’s second holiday record, following 2013’s _Wrapped In Red_.



The December after _When Christmas Comes Around_… dropped, Clarkson invited Grande to perform the track with her during her NBC holiday music special, fittingly titled _[Kelly Clarkson Presents: When Christmas Comes Around](https://www.billboard.com/music/pop/kelly-clarkson-when-christmas-comes-around-nbc-special-9655827/)_. Amy Poehler, Leslie Odom Jr., Jay Leno, Melissa McCarthy and Brett Eldredge were also featured guests on the program, which included several musical performances from the “Stronger” singer.

The audio from this performance is what now serves as the new live edition of “Santa, Can’t You Hear Me.” During the duet last year, Grande and Clarkson wore stunning white and purple gowns, respectively, and sang joyfully together while supported by a shimmering orchestra of string musicians, backup singers, percussionists and brass.



![Kelly Clarkson & Ariana Grande, "Santa, Can't You Hear Me (Live)"](https://www.billboard.com/wp-content/themes/vip/pmc-billboard-2021/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

Kelly Clarkson & Ariana Grande, “Santa, Can’t You Hear Me (Live)”Courtesy Photo

Clarkson took to Instagram Thursday (Dec. 1), exactly one year after the special aired, to direct followers to the live version of her duet with Grande, writing: It’s time, y’all! Get into the holiday spirit and listen to “Santa, Can’t You Hear Me” my duet with @arianagrande now and add it to all your holiday playlists 🎅🏼🎶.”

Watch Ariana Grande and Kelly Clarkson perform “Santa, Can’t You Hear Me” below and stream the live recording [here](https://atlantic.lnk.to/SCYHMLive).

Biography") ### Lindsay Lohan Biography by [Heather Phares](https://www.allmusic.com/author/heather-phares "View more by Heather Phares") Actress/teen pop star Lindsay Lohan entered the world of show business at the tender age of three as a Ford model, which led to television commercials for the Gap, Pizza Hut, and Wendy's. She did more television work as she grew up, including stints on soap operas like Another World and The Guiding Light, as well as roles in The Bette Show and Get a Clue, a Disney Channel movie. Lohan's Disney connection, which included starring as the twins in a remake of The Parent Trap, continued into her teens and helped her expand her career into music: along with co-starring with [Jamie Lee Curtis](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/jamie-lee-curtis-mn0001070499) in 2003's Freaky Friday, she also performed the movie's theme song, "Ultimate." [![Speak](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0001354637/front/220/Qd_CZMdONf_rivVV9EUQFCpQg_7iAU1wjqLgK_xGXts=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/speak-mw0000263426 "Speak") The following year, Lohan starred in Confessions of a Teenage Drama Queen and contributed two songs to its soundtrack. Buoyed by these successes as well as her starring role in Mean Girls, Lohan hosted the 2004 MTV Movie Awards and won an award for Female Breakout Star. She also signed to [Tommy Mottola](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/tommy-mottola-mn0001228360)'s Casablanca Records, releasing her debut album, [Speak](https://www.allmusic.com/album/speak-mw0000263426), in December of 2004. The next year saw celebrity start to catch up with Lohan. While she continued her relationship with Disney, filming a remake of Herbie: Fully Loaded, Internet and tabloid rumors spread about everything from her health and love life (she's dating Wilmer, she isn't dating Wilmer....) to her late-night party habits and diva behavior. It didn't help that [Speak](https://www.allmusic.com/album/speak-mw0000263426) was less than a success. [![A Little More Personal (Raw)](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0000343099/front/220/N43uhAJi7os6CyNZknYiRwSijaXJlYnq0St31qpAJWo=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/a-little-more-personal-raw-mw0000260413 "A Little More Personal (Raw)") By the end of 2005 Lohan's persona as the wild and damaged teen siren -- whatever its ratio of truth to fiction -- had outshone her accomplishments as an actress and a singer. And it was into this caustic tabloid climate that she released her second album, [A Little More Personal (Raw)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/a-little-more-personal-raw-mw0000260413). Though the album was critically panned, it was certified gold early in 2006. Later that year, Lohan was switched from Casablanca to Motown Records by Universal Music Group. Though she focused more on her film career in 2006 and 2007 and continued to have a swirl of tabloid attention and media controversy around her -- including her arrest on May 26, 2007, for suspicion of driving under the influence and a subsequent stay at Malibu, CA's Promises Treatment Center -- Lohan planned work on a third album in the second half of 2007. ## [Lindsay Lohan Discography](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/lindsay-lohan-mn0000831733\#discography "Lindsay Lohan Discography") Main AlbumsSingles & EPsAll Year (Oldest to Newest)Year (Newest to Oldest)AllMusic Rating (Highest to Lowest)AllMusic Rating (Lowest to Highest)User Ratings (Highest to Lowest)User Ratings (Lowest to Highest)Album Title (A-Z)Album Title (Z-A) | | Year | Credit | AllMusic Rating | User Rating | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [![Speak](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0001354637/front/120/Qd_CZMdONf_rivVV9EUQFCpQg_7iAU1wjqLgK_xGXts=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/speak-mw0000263426 "Speak") | 2004 | [Speak](https://www.allmusic.com/album/speak-mw0000263426 "Speak")

# KIM WILDE

Kim Wilde was born Kim Smith on November 18, 1960 in Chiswick, Middlesex and is an English pop singer, author, DJ and television presenter. Kim Wilde began her music career providing backing vocals for her dad Marty Wilde, and in 1980 at the age of 20 she signed to RAK Records. Kim Wilde’s chart life kicked off with her debut single Kids In America reaching Number two in the UK Official Singles chart in 1981, which was co-written with her brother Ricky Wilde. Kim Wilde won the BRIT Award for Best British Female solo artist in 1983, is a two-time winner of the Smash Hits Most Fanciable Female accolade and became the most-charted British female solo act of the 1980s. A keen gardener, Kim Wilde has written two books about the subject and presented a garden makeover show.

## [Engelbert Humperdinck Biography](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/engelbert-humperdinck-mn0000098081\#biography "Engelbert Humperdinck Biography")

### Engelbert Humperdinck Biography  by   [Steve Huey](https://www.allmusic.com/author/steve-huey "View more by Steve Huey")

Ultrasmooth balladeer Engelbert Humperdinck was often billed as "The King of Romance," and for millions of fans around the world, he more than lived up to that title. Despite the strange name and the latter-day ads hawking his music on late-night TV, Humperdinck was one of the finest middle of the road balladeers around, a sensitive lyric interpreter with excellent vocal technique and a three-and-a-half-octave vocal range. During his heyday in the late '60s and early '70s, Humperdinck cultivated the image of a mysterious heartthrob, sporting shaggy sideburns and a flamboyant wardrobe that, when coupled with his rich, silky crooning, drove female fans wild. He was especially popular in Europe and his native U.K., and his worldwide record sales -- counting both albums and singles -- eventually totaled well over 100 million. Like his friendly rival [Tom Jones](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/tom-jones-mn0000609396) (with whom he shared a manager for many years), he later settled into a comfortable niche as a stalwart of the Las Vegas entertainment circuit.

Humperdinck was born Arnold George Dorsey on May 2, 1936, in Madras, India. His father worked as an engineer for the British Army, and the family returned to England when Arnold was seven, settling in Leicester. He took up the saxophone at age 11, but didn't really try his hand at singing until 17, when his friends talked him into entering a small local singing contest. Not only did he earn a standing ovation, he also impressed the audience with a knack for comic impressions, particularly [Jerry Lewis](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/jerry-lewis-mn0000278559) (which he often included in his later live shows). In fact, his [Lewis](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/lewis-mn0000278559) impression gave him his first stage name, Gerry Dorsey. He started singing in nightclubs, but after finishing school, he put his budding music career on hold to serve in the military through 1956.

When Dorsey returned, he got the chance to record for Decca in 1958, but the lone single released, "I'll Never Fall in Love Again," flopped. He managed a few appearances on British television, most prominently on the show Oh, Boy!, and toured with [Marty Wilde](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/marty-wilde-mn0000375239); the exposure helped him become a popular concert attraction in his own right, even though he had no hits of his own. His career was nearly derailed in 1961 when he contracted tuberculosis, which kept him completely out of commission for six months; once he recovered, he found that England's burgeoning rock & roll movement was pushing more traditional pop out of the spotlight.

As Gerry Dorsey, he struggled for several years until he got in touch with former roommate [Gordon Mills](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/gordon-mills-mn0000557506) in 1965. Once the lead singer of a skiffle group called [the Viscounts](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/the-viscounts-mn0002032177), [Mills](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/mills-mn0000557506) had moved into artist management, and at the time was enjoying breakout success with [Tom Jones](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/tom-jones-mn0000609396). It was [Mills](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/mills-mn0000557506) who suggested that Dorsey change his name to the well-nigh unforgettable Engelbert Humperdinck, after the 19th century Austrian composer who adapted Hansel and Gretel into an opera. To create an air of mystery around the singer, [Mills](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/mills-mn0000557506) insisted that he refrain from any contact with his fans following concerts, even if that meant escaping through windows. The gimmicks worked, as the newly christened Humperdinck scored a new deal with Decca. His first two singles, "Dommage Dommage" and "Stay," were released in 1966, and both missed the charts. Biography](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/band-aid-mn0000116630\#biography "Band Aid Biography") ### Band Aid Biography by [Timothy Monger](https://www.allmusic.com/author/timothy-monger "View more by Timothy Monger") Charity supergroup Band Aid was formed in London, England in 1984 by [Boomtown Rats](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/boomtown-rats-mn0000520033) frontman [Bob Geldof](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/bob-geldof-mn0000801971) and producer [Midge Ure](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/midge-ure-mn0000479687). Intended to fund anti-poverty efforts in Ethiopia, the ensemble recorded the single "Do They Know It's Christmas?" for release during the 1984 holiday season. Aided by vocal efforts from [Bono](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/bono-mn0000771269), [Sting](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/sting-mn0000522377), [George Michael](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/george-michael-mn0000545074), [Boy George](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/boy-george-mn0000771470), Simon Le Bon, and a host of other contemporary pop stars of the day, the single topped the pop charts, becoming the number one Christmas single of the year and raising more than $24,000,000 for its cause. Such was Band Aid's success, several other celebrity-aided organizations launched fundraising campaigns the following year resulting in the star-studded Live Aid concert and the American charity supergroup [USA for Africa](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/usa-for-africa-mn0001775564). # UNDERNEATH THE TREE  by [KELLY CLARKSON](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/13611/kelly-clarkson/)

* * *

Underneath The Tree is taken from Kelly Clarkson's sixth studio album Wrapped In Red.

The sparkly festive favourite was originally released in 2013 when it charted at a modest Number 30, but slowly but surely went on to be adopted by the British public as a contemporary seasonal staple.

Written by Kelly Clarkson and Greg Kurstin, Underneath The Tree's peak position on the Official Chart has steadily climbed and climbed since its release, and on 13 December 2024 [Underneath The Tree](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/wham-last-christmas-number-1-return/ "Underneath The Tree goes Top 10") finally broke the UK Top 10 for the first time after eleven years on chart.

See the rise of Underneath The Tree as a modern festive classic.

## Summary

- Singer Chris Rea, known for hits including [Driving Home for Christmas](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0q5g3v02qjt?post=asset%3A17bae92f-9b7e-4830-a94d-db35944f1466#post), has died aged 74

- As well as his much-loved festive hit, Rea had success in the late 1970s and 1980s withFool (If You Think It's Over), Let's Dance and The Road To Hell

- "He passed away peacefully in hospital earlier today following a short illness, surrounded by his family," [a statement from his wife and two children says](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0q5g3v02qjt?post=asset%3A53055720-6d66-4ac0-ac2e-c9c77918f44c#post)

- The musician was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer aged 33, had his pancreas removed in 2001, [and later said he took 34 pills every day](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0q5g3v02qjt?post=asset%3Ae045897d-2cbb-41b2-ab6c-d4a56e9dc5ab#post)

- Rea was born in Middlesbrough to an Italian father and Irish mother - his family were in the ice cream business, [and Rea even took his driving test in his dad's ice cream van](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0q5g3v02qjt?post=asset%3Adef6c5f8-4444-4c39-be14-6659d6ecc086#post)

- Releasing Driving Home for Christmas was his record company's decision: "I did everything I could to get them not to release that record," he said later. ["Thankfully they did"](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0q5g3v02qjt?post=asset%3Ae2ea51bc-46e2-4ea5-8865-4dac95c2fc57#post)

- He also said he was on the dole when he wrote the song - [and banned from driving](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0q5g3v02qjt?post=asset%3A38b2cace-7c2e-4f7e-bc67-ab752ba96e34#post)


## Live Reporting

Edited by Jack Burgess

## LIVE stream page 1

01. ![](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/128/cpsprodpb//vivo/live/images/2024/11/21/efc4785b-e209-4310-bc20-65148f0cfca4.jpg.webp)**Adam Goldsmith**

    Live reporter



    ![Chris Rea pictured in 2005](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/640/cpsprodpb/vivo/live/images/2025/12/22/f1c7be93-cc5d-4532-b510-567e8544b00d.jpg.webp)Image source, Getty Images



    Singer Chris Rea, widely known for the festive hit Driving Home for Christmas, has died aged 74, his family confirmed today.



    A somewhat reluctant popstar, the Middlesbrough native was shy of the spotlight, and even [admitted rallying against the record label's decision](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0q5g3v02qjt?post=asset%3Ae2ea51bc-46e2-4ea5-8865-4dac95c2fc57#post) to release his biggest hit - though accepted he was thankful when they eventually did in 1986.



    The drive-time anthem came to exist while Rea was on a driving ban - [more on that in our earlier post](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0q5g3v02qjt?post=asset%3A38b2cace-7c2e-4f7e-bc67-ab752ba96e34#post).



    Reluctant or otherwise, he [even resisted a more marketable name swap](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0q5g3v02qjt?post=asset%3Aaf866f4c-1517-4bfb-a212-cd30d5f1bb02#post), the fame the track brought Rea is indisputable; nearly 40 years on, the [single took a spot at 30](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0q5g3v02qjt?post=asset%3A17bae92f-9b7e-4830-a94d-db35944f1466#post) in this year's UK Christmas top 40.



    A proud guitarist with influences stretching deep into the blues, Rea recorded 25 solo albums, two of which topped the UK albums chart.



    ![Chris Rea on a bike next to an ice cream van](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/640/cpsprodpb/vivo/live/images/2025/12/22/396b6b4f-1165-4208-b02f-22d47fbb037c.jpg.webp)Image source, Getty Images

    Image caption,



    Aged 22, Rea promotes his single So Much Love while working for his father's ice cream company





    Rea's success came [despite the singer suffering a string of health issues](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0q5g3v02qjt?post=asset%3Ae045897d-2cbb-41b2-ab6c-d4a56e9dc5ab#post). A pancreatic cancer diagnosis at just 33-years-old was followed by operations on his liver and then a stroke later in life.



    [Tributes have been coming in](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0q5g3v02qjt?post=asset%3A34b0cac6-8173-4007-a8c9-25dace12de26#post) since his family announced Rea's death in hospital following a short illness earlier today.



    "Chris’s music has created the soundtrack to many lives, and his legacy will live on through the songs he leaves behind," a post on his social media accounts reads.



    - _We're closing our live coverage now... but you can_ [read more on Chris Rea's life in our full obituary](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c51y93wqv5po)

02. ![Television presenter Timmy Mallett](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/640/cpsprodpb/vivo/live/images/2025/12/22/cea70ce2-0787-4037-b194-d1cd3a1660fe.jpg.webp)Image source, Getty Images



    We've just seen a tribute from television presenter Timmy Mallett.



    "Chris is driving home for Christmas now singing for our nearest & dearest," Mallett says in a post on social media platform X.



    Mallett also says he bought Rea's home in 1991, and adds that a "happy Christmas" message written by his daughters is still sprayed on the garage wall.



    "Grateful for his wonderful gravely voice. God bless you Chris," Mallett says.

    Middlesbrough-born Chris Rea found fame in the '70s and '80s and had two UK number one studio albums.



    He performed all over the globe during his career, including numerous times for the BBC.



    ![Rea performing on stage, circa 1980](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/640/cpsprodpb/vivo/live/images/2025/12/22/50b61558-ffa3-4b42-9157-b7abcedb6011.jpg.webp)Image source, Getty Images

    His love of driving inspired many of his songs - here Rea's pictured playing at the BBC in 2009

    Image caption,



    Chris Rea stands between former Formula One racing drivers Olivier Panis and Ralf Schumacher at Silverstone in 2006





    Away from music, Rea was a vehicle addict - he owned and raced several vintage cars, including a 1957 Morris Minor 1000 police car.



    The singer was friends with Eddie Jordan, who owned the Jordan Grand Prix Formula One team, and he once even helped out in the pit lane.



    "I had the whole uniform," he said. "He put me in charge of the tyre-warmer for the rear right tyre of Eddie Irvine's car."



    Rea was also friends with former British racing driver Nigel Mansell and gifted him a copy of his record The Road to Hell following a serious crash.

    Tributes are continuing to come in from Chris Rea's friends and colleagues since the announcement of his death.



    Here are some that we've seen so far:



    - **Middlesbrough FC** says the football club is “deeply saddened” by Rea’s death and call him [a “Teesside icon”](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0q5g3v02qjt?post=asset%3Ac5d2a8bd-3b20-432e-b174-141e965f6f09#post)
    - **The mayor of Rea’s hometown** says the singer [“helped put Middlesbrough on the map”](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0q5g3v02qjt?post=asset%3A9121b298-2f29-4dfc-923e-bba483c354ec#post)
    - **TV personality Lizzie Cundy** explains that Rea will ["always be an inspiration and legend to me"](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0q5g3v02qjt?post=asset%3A34b0cac6-8173-4007-a8c9-25dace12de26#post). ## [Bastille Biography](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/bastille-mn0002825814\#biography "Bastille Biography")

### Bastille Biography  by   [Heather Phares](https://www.allmusic.com/author/heather-phares "View more by Heather Phares")

[![Bad Blood](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0003885782/front/220/mNxBxwiRB61TP0tEXpTaHj6KsMttLlyBmmVTZ6_CLs0=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/bad-blood-mw0002486836 "Bad Blood")
Originally the solo project of London-based singer/songwriter [Dan Smith](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/dan-smith-mn0002833952), Bastille combine glossy '80s synth textures and arena-friendly choruses into dramatic yet earnest, brooding yet joyful songs like their hit single "Pompeii," which helped them sell millions of copies of their 2013 debut album, [Bad Blood](https://www.allmusic.com/album/bad-blood-mw0002486836). Later on, the band expanded and refined their approach. For 2016's [Wild World](https://www.allmusic.com/album/wild-world-mw0002960536), they added hints of R&B, dance, and rock, as well as overtly political songwriting, then took a conceptual and confessional approach on 2019's gospel- and house music-influenced [Doom Days](https://www.allmusic.com/album/doom-days-mw0003274304). With the dystopian fantasies and realities of 2022's [Give Me the Future](https://www.allmusic.com/album/give-me-the-future-mw0003609040) and the collaborative song stories of 2024's four-part [& \[Ampersand\]](https://www.allmusic.com/album/-ampersand--mw0004349702), Bastille continued to make pop music that was equally ambitious and relatable.

[![The Laura Palmer EP](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0003484022/front/220/gNa1pHAQqFTQG5n7RTmkEgSijaXJlYnq0St31qpAJWo=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/the-laura-palmer-ep-mw0002239497 "The Laura Palmer EP")
Born in Leeds, England, to South African parents, [Smith](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/smith-mn0002833952) began writing songs at age 15. However, he didn't share his music until several years later, when a friend encouraged him to enter 2007's Leeds Bright Young Things competition. After placing as a finalist, he continued to work on music on his own and with [To Kill a King](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/to-kill-a-king-mn0002677665)'s [Ralph Pelleymounter](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/ralph-pelleymounter-mn0002810563) while studying at the University of Leeds. After he graduated, [Smith](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/smith-mn0002833952) moved to London and pursued music in earnest. In 2010, he connected with drummer Chris Wood, guitarist/bassist [William Farquarson](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/william-farquarson-mn0003162294), and keyboardist [Kyle Simmons](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/kyle-simmons-mn0003257210). Taking their name from Bastille Day -- which also happens to be [Smith](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/smith-mn0002833952)'s birthday -- the group became Bastille. That July, they released their debut 7" single, [Flaws/Icarus](https://www.allmusic.com/album/flaws-icarus-mw0002217536), in a limited edition of 300 through the indie label Young and Lost Club. The following year, Bastille self-released the [Laura Palmer](https://www.allmusic.com/album/laura-palmer-mw0002239497) EP, which reflected [Smith](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/smith-mn0002833952)'s fondness for the cult TV series Twin Peaks.

[![VS. (Other People's Heartache, Pt. III)](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0004341590/front/220/DqAKaaWiuJRya1kmlwsJwg4Q1ghY8VaPylnm7PwcKNY=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/vs-other-peoples-heartache-pt-iii-mw0002771787 "VS. (Other People's Heartache, Pt. III)")
In December 2011, Bastille signed to EMI and made their debut on the label with the April 2012 single "Overjoyed." That August, "Bad Blood" marked the band's first appearance on the U.K. charts, peaking at number 90. In October 2012, EMI's re-release of "Flaws" became their first single to debut in the Top 40. Bastille's breakthrough came with "Pompeii," which reached number two on the U.K. charts in February 2013 and number five on Billboard's Hot 100 singles chart a month later. Also in March 2013, the band's first full-length, [Bad Blood](https://www.allmusic.com/album/bad-blood-mw0002486836), arrived, debuting at the top of the U.K. albums chart. # ED SHEERAN & ELTON JOHN

Ed Sheeran and Elton John joined forces for the first time in 2021 for the festive single Merry Christmas. Born out of the duo's friendship (and a phone call Ed received from Elton on Christmas Day 2020), Merry Christmas debuted at Number 1 on the Official Singles Chart, giving Ed his 12th UK Number 1 and Elton his ninth.

# Kylie Minogue sleighs her way to 11th UK Number 1 album with Kylie Christmas (Fully Wrapped)

## Kylie pulls level with the likes of David Bowie and Eminem in the artists with most UK Number 1 albums

![Kylie Minogue Fully Wrapped Number 1 Album](https://www.officialcharts.com/sites/default/files/styles/content_column_mobile/public/2025-12/Kylie%20Minogue%20Fully%20Wrapped%20Number%201%20Album.jpg?itok=IDLzBUup)

[Kylie Minogue](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/43484/kylie/) is gifted an early XMAS present, sleighing her way to secure this week’s Official Number 1 with [Kylie Christmas (Fully Wrapped)](https://www.officialcharts.com/albums/kylie-minogue-kylie-christmas-fully-wrapped/).

A reissue of her 2015 release [Kylie Christmas](https://www.officialcharts.com/albums/kylie-minogue-kylie-christmas/), which originally peaked at Number 12, Kylie celebrates her 11th UK Number 1 album, taking her level with the likes of [David Bowie](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/19138/david-bowie/), [Eminem](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/7507/eminem/) and [Rod Stewart](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/20537/rod-stewart/) in the league of artists with the most UK Number 1 albums.

A fitting way to begin the festive fun as the Christmas Number 1 race kicks off today, could it be an indicator of what's to come next week? With limited edition vinyl and signed CD versions of Kylie’s single XMAS dropping today, all eyes will be on the Aussie pop princess as a key contender in the biggest chart race of the year.

Kylie Christmas (Fully Wrapped) also tops the [Official Album Vinyl Chart](https://www.officialcharts.com/charts/vinyl-albums-chart/), shifting the most copies on wax over the past seven days, as well as the [Official Record Store Chart](https://www.officialcharts.com/charts/record-store-chart/), crowned the most popular album in UK independent record shops this week.

![Kylie Minogue Fully Wrapped Number 1 Album Christmas](https://www.officialcharts.com/sites/default/files/styles/content_column_mobile/public/2025-12/Kylie%20Minogue%20Fully%20Wrapped%20Number%201%20Album%20Christmas.jpg?itok=1wIE88ei)

### MORE: [Your 2025 Christmas Number 1 contenders](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/christmas-number-1-2025-contenders-songs/)

With the deluxe version of Mercury Prize-winning album [People Watching](https://www.officialcharts.com/albums/sam-fender-people-watching/), Geordie giant [Sam Fender](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/54705/sam-fender/) sees the record jump an impressive 31 places back into the Top 5 (3).

Dubbed one of the sets of the Glastonbury 2025 weekend, [Olivia Rodrigo](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/56921/olivia-rodrigo/)’s [Live From Glastonbury (A BBC Recording)](https://www.officialcharts.com/albums/olivia-rodrigo-live-from-glastonbury-a-bbc-recording/) places inside the Top 20 with the release of its physical variants (12).

[Noah Kahan](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/63540/noah-kahan/)’s former Number 1 [Stick Season](https://www.officialcharts.com/albums/noah-kahan-stick-season/) rebounds back into the Top 20 (19). [Depeche Mode](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/20192/depeche-mode/) see [Memento Mori – Mexico City](https://www.officialcharts.com/albums/depeche-mode-memento-mori-mexico-city/), the live version of their show celebrating the 2023 album Momento Mori, earns the outfit their 22nd Top 40 hit (22).

It’s a sixth Top 40 album for Rotherham rockers [The Reytons](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/59586/reytons/) with [Roll The Dice](https://www.officialcharts.com/albums/the-reytons-roll-the-dice/) (27).

American rap legend [50 Cent](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/12550/50-cent/) finds 2017 hits compilation [Best Of 50 Cent](https://www.officialcharts.com/albums/50-cent-best-of/) on the up (29), following the star’s directorial debut on documentary series, Sean Combs: The Reckoning.

[Nick Cave & The Bad Seeds](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/17740/nick-cave-and-the-bad-seeds/)’ [Live God](https://www.officialcharts.com/albums/nick-cave-the-bad-seeds-live-god/), the live version of their 2024 Top 5 project [Wild God](https://www.officialcharts.com/albums/nick-cave-the-bad-seeds-wild-god/), lands at Number 33 this week.

And finally, [Radiohead](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/28161/radiohead/)’s [OK Computer](https://www.officialcharts.com/albums/radiohead-ok-computer/) re-enters the Top 40 as the band embark on the last leg of their reunion tour in Europe this week (40).

![Kylie Minogue Fully Wrapped Number 1 Album 2](https://www.officialcharts.com/sites/default/files/styles/content_column_mobile/public/2025-12/Kylie%20Minogue%20Fully%20Wrapped%20Number%201%20Album%202.jpg?itok=Z2QkTQ8j)

### Follow the Official Christmas Number 1 race

The Official Christmas Number 1 race 2025 kicks off Friday December 12 with sales and streams counting up until midnight (11.59pm) on Thursday, December 18.

Tune in to The Official Chart on BBC Radio 1 on Friday December 19 from 3pm to hear the Christmas Top 40 countdown and the exclusive reveal of the Official Christmas Number 1 2025.

The full [Top 100 Official Christmas Singles Chart](https://www.officialcharts.com/charts/singles-chart/) and [Albums Chart](https://www.officialcharts.com/charts/albums-chart/) will be published on OfficialCharts.com from 5.45pm.

Join the conversation now using the hashtag #XmasNo1. # STAY ANOTHER DAY  by [EAST 17](https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/28015/east-17/)

* * *

East 17 are an English boy band who formed in 1991 originally comprised of Tony Mortimer, Brian Harvey, John Hendy and Terry Coldwell. Released November 21, 1994, Stay Another Day was the quartet’s tenth single and their first UK Official Singles Chart Number 1 entering the chart at Number 7 before leaping to the top for five weeks to claim 1994’s UK Official Singles Chart Christmas Number 1 despite facing stiff competition from Mariah Carey’s future canon classic, All I Want for Christmas Is You.

Co-written by Tony Mortimer (with Rob Kean and Dominic Hawken) about the suicide of his brother Ollie, it was produced by Phil Harding and Ian Curnow and was the third song issued from their second album Steam. Originally not destined for release as a Christmas single, bells were added to end of the song for it to appeal and the boys filmed two videos – one in a recording studio, and another snowy affair with them in parkas – for it to extend past the festive season for a 15-week chart life.

# SHAKIN' STEVENS

Shakin' Stevens is the moniker of Welsh pop singer Michael Baratt, one of the most popular artists of the 1980s.

Overall, Shakin' Stevens has achieved four UK Number 1 singles. One of them, Merry Christmas Everyone, is a festive staple and one of the best-selling singles in UK chart history.

Shaky has continued an enviable output in his twilight years, achieving a sixth UK Top 10 album in 2020, six decades into his career. (Image: Andre Csillag/Shutterstock)

"Welcome to the Pleasuredome") Best remembered as the frontman for British pop phenomenon [Frankie Goes to Hollywood](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/frankie-goes-to-hollywood-mn0000139741), singer Holly Johnson was born February 9, 1960 in Liverpool; in 1977 he joined the short-lived [Big in Japan](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/big-in-japan-mn0000062500), and after issuing a pair of solo singles, "Yankee Rose" and "Hobo Joe," he formed [Frankie Goes to Hollywood](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/frankie-goes-to-hollywood-mn0000139741) in 1980. Buffering their epic, opulent dance-pop with a brilliant marketing campaign highlighted by a series of provocative videos and sloganeering T-shirts, [Frankie](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/frankie-mn0000165855) remains one of the '80s quintessential bands, although their success proved short-lived and never really translated across the Atlantic; they rose to superstardom on the strength of the singles "Relax," "Two Tribes," and "The Power of Love." Their 1984 debut, [Welcome to the Pleasuredome](https://www.allmusic.com/album/welcome-to-the-pleasuredome-mw0000189928), was also well-received by the press, but the group's fall was as meteoric as their rise; after a less successful 1986 effort, [Liverpool](https://www.allmusic.com/album/liverpool-mw0000650165), they disbanded. Johnson then spent the next several years locked in a court battle against label ZTT, ultimately winning his artistic freedom; he returned to music in 1989 with his solo debut [Blast](https://www.allmusic.com/album/blast-mw0000200779), which topped the U.K. charts. [Dreams That Money Can't Buy](https://www.allmusic.com/album/dreams-that-money-cant-buy-mw0000886987) followed two years later, around the time the openly homosexual singer discovered he'd contracted HIV, a subject frankly detailed in his 1994 autobiography A Bone in My Flute. Also a successful painter, in 1996 Johnson exhibited his work in London; forming his own record label, Pleasuredome, in 1999 he issued his third LP, [Soulstream](https://www.allmusic.com/album/soulstream-mw0000948512). Fifteen years later, the single "Follow Your Heart" arrived along with the full-length LP [Europa](https://www.allmusic.com/album/europa-mw0002698492). The album and accompanying tour marked 30 years since the release of [Frankie](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/frankie-mn0000165855)'s [Welcome to the Pleasuredome](https://www.allmusic.com/album/welcome-to-the-pleasuredome-mw0000189928). ## [Holly Johnson Discography](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/mn0000685396\#discography "Holly Johnson Discography") Main AlbumsCompilationsSingles & EPsAll Year (Oldest to Newest)Year (Newest to Oldest)AllMusic Rating (Highest to Lowest)AllMusic Rating (Lowest to Highest)User Ratings (Highest to Lowest)User Ratings (Lowest to Highest)Album Title (A-Z)Album Title (Z-A) | | Year | Credit | AllMusic Rating | User Rating | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [![Blast](https://fastly-s3.allmusic.com/release/mr0002858926/front/120/1DUJj4It9jBKAVBWG6GbM5hUoDg0hsvx4F4sL4oO-nA=.jpg)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/blast-mw0000200779 "Blast") | 1989 | [Blast](https://www.allmusic.com/album/blast-mw0000200779 "Blast")

# The Beach Boys' Christmas Album

[The Beach Boys](https://music.apple.com/us/artist/the-beach-boys/562555)

Holiday · 1964

Opening with five Beach Boys originals (including "Christmas Day," with Al Jardine's first lead vocal), _The Beach Boys' Christmas Album_ starts like any other Beach Boys album, with tight-knit harmonies and a pop-rock band providing the instrumental backing. The remaining seven standards, however, include The Four Freshmen's arranger, Dick Reynolds, handling the orchestral backing for tunes such as "Frosty the Snowman," "We Three Kings of Orient Are," and "White Christmas." The mix between the joyful and the solemn makes for a well-rounded collection for those who enjoy holiday fare. "Auld Lang Syne" is an interesting a cappella piece arranged by Brian Wilson, interrupted briefly by Denny Wilson wishing everyone a Merry Christmas on behalf of the band.

Lowe](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/nick-lowe-mn0000866841 "Nick Lowe") ## [Jona Lewie Biography](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/jona-lewie-mn0000822398\#biography "Jona Lewie Biography") ### Jona Lewie Biography by [Steve Huey](https://www.allmusic.com/author/steve-huey "View more by Steve Huey") While he wasn't one of the biggest names on Stiff Records, Jona Lewie was one of those irrepressible characters who gave the pioneering British indie label its utterly unique flavor. Born John Lewis, Lewie got his start in the early-'70s pub rock scene, playing keyboards for the Sussex group Brett Marvin & the Thunderbolts. Bizarrely, the group enjoyed its greatest success under the Lewie-helmed alias Terry Dactyl & the Dinosaurs, scoring a U.K. Top Five hit in 1972 with "Seaside Shuffle." However, subsequent releases under the name failed to duplicate that success, and Lewie departed the band. He resurfaced on Stiff in 1978 as a solo artist, singing pub rock and new wave tunes in a dry, deadpan, Ian Dury-ish voice. Most distinctive was his simultaneous taste for musical nostalgia (British music hall, skiffle, etc.), as evidenced on several cuts from his debut album, On the Other Hand There's a Fist. Lewie also participated in the 1978 Be Stiff package tour (the label's second). In 1980, Lewie scored a Top 20 U.K. hit with the self-effacing single "You'll Always Find Me in the Kitchen at Parties," which, according to legend, was backing vocalist Kirsty MacColl's first session for the label. Lewie trumped it several months later with "Stop the Cavalry," a strange blend of anti-war protest, brass band arrangements, and Christmas sentiment. Surprisingly, the single hit the Top Five and became something of a Christmas standard in the U.K., where it was trotted out every holiday season and featured on numerous Christmas compilations. Stiff rushed out another album, 1981's Heart Skips Beat, to capitalize, but lightning would only strike twice, and Lewie issued his last single in 1983. ## [Jona Lewie Discography](https://www.allmusic.com/artist/jona-lewie-mn0000822398\#discography "Jona Lewie Discography") Main AlbumsCompilationsSingles & EPsAll Year (Oldest to Newest)Year (Newest to Oldest)AllMusic Rating (Highest to Lowest)AllMusic Rating (Lowest to Highest)User Ratings (Highest to Lowest)User Ratings (Lowest to Highest)Album Title (A-Z)Album Title (Z-A) | | Year | Credit | AllMusic Rating | User Rating | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [![Alias Jona Lewie](https://fastly-gce.allmusic.com/images/no_image/album_100x100.png)](https://www.allmusic.com/album/alias-jona-lewie-mw0000858358 "Alias Jona Lewie") | 1980 | [Alias Jona Lewie](https://www.allmusic.com/album/alias-jona-lewie-mw0000858358 "Alias Jona Lewie")

## about Brenda Lee

Brenda Lee signed with the legendary Decca Records label before her 12th birthday and went on to record such landmark hits as “Sweet Nothin’s,” “All Alone Am I,” “Break it to Me Gently,” “I’m Sorry” and of course, the perennial holiday favorite “Rockin’ Around the Christmas Tree.”

Throughout her career she shared stages and earned the respect of the world’s most revered performers. The Beatles opened for her and the lads from Liverpool became good friends with the Southern belle from Atlanta. Elvis Presley and Lee made their Grand Ole Opry debut on the same night. “I’ll never forget, he came in and they sent him down to that men’s shop in the arcade to get a tux. They said he wasn’t dressed right, so here he comes back with a tux. He wow’d the audience. He tore the house down and I’ll never forget they told him to keep his day job,” she says shaking her head. Incredible talent, hard work and a humble attitude are the cornerstones of Lee’s impressive career.

**Deana Martin** swings into the Season with **White Christmas**, a ring-a-ding collection of Yuletide favorites worthy of Deana’s Rat Pack showbiz heritage. From the start, Deana sets the tone with “I’ve Got My Love to Keep Me Warm”… _and the season sizzles from there!_  Drawing from Holiday favorites, some previously recorded by her Dad, Dean Martin, Uncle Frank (Sinatra) and Uncle Sammy (yes, THAT Sam), **Deana Martin** delivers ten solid performances worthy of _everyone’s_ Christmas listen list.  On Irving Berlin’s cherished classic, “White Christmas”, Deana is joined by legendary entertainer Andy Williams.  The meeting of these two voices makes for an instant Christmas classic.  **White Christmas** by **Deana Martin** is one of the most refreshingly creative and swinging Christmas releases in years; a five-star festival of holiday cheer!

**Deana Martin** is the daughter of the master himself, Dean Martin, and she has long carried on his legacy–and built one of her own–singing the songs the Rat Pack made famous in the sound and style we’ve all loved ever since.

For this Christmas set, that means nothing but the Christmas songs you know and love–some with hot swingin’ and sexy arrangements and some with that easy, relaxed, and sweet sentimentality (for which I believe her father held the original patent).  This is a Christmas album the way they _used to_ make them, with classy and classic big band arrangements and vocals that drip like honey from your speakers, tasting every bit as sweet.
